translation: Target is the proposition that for every arithmetic axiom set T and every Δ₁ presentation of T, if every sentence in T is true in the standard natural numbers, then the union of T with all local reflection axioms for T is consistent (does not derive a contradiction). There is one such axiom for every arithmetic sentence σ, whether or not σ belongs to T: it is the implication Prov_T(⌜σ⌝) → σ, using the provability predicate for T itself, not for the augmented theory. The truth hypothesis is stated for the axioms in T; T need not be deductively closed or extend any specified base theory.

divergences.description: Chalmers concludes that the augmented system is sound: every theorem it proves is true. The target concludes only that the augmented system is consistent. Soundness implies consistency, but consistency does not imply soundness.

The parenthetical applies to any true statement, and the particular statement Chalmers adds is “I am F,” an identity claim. The target instead adds a fixed schema: all instances of Prov_T(⌜σ⌝) → σ at once. These are true under the hypothesis on T, but the target neither treats an arbitrary true addition nor represents the identity claim.

The target restricts the systems to Δ₁-presented theories of first-order arithmetic and interprets truth in the standard natural numbers. The parenthetical states no such restrictions. Def3 T expresses soundness via truth of the axioms, which suffices for truth of all theorems by soundness of first-order deduction.
The target has no agent or notion of knowledge, so it does not express Chalmers's surrounding inference to “I know that the larger system F' is sound.” The parenthetical itself is not epistemic.

judgement.summary: The target gives a related consistency claim for one specific extension by true axioms. It does not state Chalmers's principle that adding a true statement preserves soundness or formalize his application of that principle to “I am F.”
